persona_reviews.likely_action: Skims the four cards, maybe opens one demo, then leaves without filling the form because nothing signals how fast a site could actually be turned around.
objections: I need a site up fast and this page tells me nothing about turnaround time.
The primary CTA is 'Request your preview' but I don't know how long a preview takes or what happens after.
No phone, no scheduling, no 'reply within X' — the next step feels slow and open-ended.
trust_gaps: No timeline, availability, or response-time promise anywhere on the page.
No indication these demos were built quickly or that BBW can move fast for me.
No proof a real person responds — only a footer line saying it's one person, which could read as 'might be slow / one-man bottleneck.'
useful_rewrites: Add a turnaround line near the CTA: 'Most previews are ready within 2-3 days. Request yours and I'll reply personally within a day.'
Change 'Request your preview' to 'Get my free preview (usually 2-3 days)' so the speed is explicit.
Add a one-line 'what happens next' under the CTA so the urgent buyer can see the path is short.
clarity_notes: 'Request your preview' is ambiguous — is the preview free, paid, fast, slow? Urgent buyers won't infer it.
The page is a gallery with no time/availability cues, so an urgent buyer has no anchor to act on.

persona_reviews.likely_action: Opens two or three demos to inspect quality, finds them generic with placeholder business names, and bounces to compare against named agencies with real case studies and testimonials.
objections: These are made-up businesses (Ironside Auto Works, Pelican & Lime) — I can't verify any of this is real client work.

The page tells me nothing about credentials, process, or what's actually included.
trust_gaps: Demos are fictional concepts, not real shipped clients, and the page doesn't even claim a single real customer.
Zero third-party proof: no reviews, ratings, logos, or outcomes.
No detail on what BBW actually does, how, or to what standard — the copy is atmospheric ('restaurant energy') rather than evidentiary.
useful_rewrites: Label honestly and add proof: 'These are concept demos I built. Want to see a real client site? [link]' — then show at least one real launched site.
Add a short 'What you get' list under the grid (pages, mobile, basic SEO, revisions) so the work is verifiable in scope.
Add 1-2 testimonials or a 'built for [real business]' credit even if just one exists.
clarity_notes: 'Four previews with real range' uses 'real' while every example is fictional — that word choice undercuts credibility for a careful reader.
Copy like 'restaurant energy' and 'real customer' is vibe, not evidence; a skeptic reads it as filler.

persona_reviews.likely_action: Likes the personal 'one person' framing but finds no face, no story, no vouching proof, so doesn't feel confident enough to reach out unprompted.
